questions.q: What does an API gateway typically do?
o: One entry point that routes calls and handles auth and rate limits
A central store holding the data for every service
A replacement for service discovery inside the cluster
A place that runs the business logic of every service
questions.w: It hides the internal topology from clients. Keep business logic out of it to avoid a distributed monolith.

questions.q: A downstream service is failing and slow. What does a circuit breaker do?
o: Stops calling for a while and fails fast, then probes for recovery
Retries as fast as possible until a response arrives
Restarts the failing downstream service itself
Caches every response for ever after
questions.w: States are closed, open and half-open. Failing fast frees threads and gives the failing service room to recover.

questions.q: Why is retrying a failed call with no delay dangerous?
o: It can overload a struggling service; use backoff with jitter
Retries are not allowed over HTTP at all
Retries always create duplicate data
Retries automatically disable the circuit breaker
questions.w: Synchronised retries create a retry storm. Backoff spreads load and jitter stops clients from retrying in lockstep. Retry only idempotent calls.

questions.q: What does the bulkhead pattern protect against?
o: One slow dependency using all threads and sinking the service
Data being lost after a disk failure
Unauthorised users reaching internal services
Version mismatches between two deployed services
questions.w: Isolating resources (separate pools per dependency) contains the failure, like watertight compartments in a ship.

questions.q: Which statement about the database-per-service pattern is correct?
o: Each service owns its data; others use its API or events
All services share one schema for easy joins
Services read each other's tables directly for speed
Only a single service is allowed a database
questions.w: It enables independent deployment and scaling, but cross-service queries and consistency need new patterns such as sagas and CQRS views.

o: Services find the current network locations of other services
Services are scanned automatically for security flaws
Request latency is measured for every call
Service traffic is encrypted in transit
questions.w: Instances come and go. A registry (Eureka, Consul) or the platform DNS (Kubernetes services) keeps track of healthy instances.

questions.q: What is the strangler fig pattern used for?
o: Gradually replace a legacy system by routing slices to new services
Kill any request that takes too long to be answered
Compress the responses coming from the older services
Rewrite everything and release it in a single big bang
questions.w: A facade routes some traffic to the new code while the rest still hits the old system, until the old one can be switched off.

o: The model that writes (commands) from the model that reads (queries)
The front end of an app from its back end
Test code from the production code that it checks
Public APIs from the private APIs of a service
questions.w: Read models can be denormalised and scaled on their own, updated from events. It adds eventual consistency, so use it where reads and writes differ a lot.
